This challenge explores all matches of Italian soccer Serie A league from 1993 to current year. The dataset is contained in the website [football-data.co.uk](http://www.football-data.co.uk/italym.php). 

### Challenges
1. Think about how to scrape the data from the website, but write no code at this stage.
1. Ask AI to write code to import data by scraping the website. Select only columns Date, HomeTeam, AwayTeam, FTHG (home team goals), FTAG (away team goals)  and filter rows with a valid (not NA) Date. 
1. Using dplyr and tidyr packages (no for loops!), compute statistics for every team (matches, wins, loses, draws, points, points per match). Hint: mutate a column with the outcome of the match (for instance, H = home teams wins, A = away team wins, P = draw). Then group by team and outcome (home and away) and hence spread the outcome. Do this step without the use of AI.
1. Come up with at least 3 data questions on the data at hand. Just write the questions, do not find the answers.

### Setup
```{r eval=TRUE, echo=TRUE}
library(rvest)
library(readr)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(purrr)
library(lubridate)
```


### Scraping only link relative to Serie A 
```{r eval=TRUE, echo=TRUE}
base_url <- "http://www.football-data.co.uk/"
page_url <- paste0(base_url, "italym.php")

serie_a_urls <- read_html(page_url) |>
  # Using XPath to select only the links that contain "I1.csv" and have the text "Serie A"
  html_elements(xpath = "//a[contains(@href, 'I1.csv') and text() = 'Serie A']") |>
  html_attr("href") |>
  url_absolute(base_url)
serie_a_urls

```

### Download, select columns, create a tibble and filter rows with valid Date
```{r eval=TRUE, echo=TRUE}
serie_a_df <- serie_a_urls |>
  map(\(url) {
    read_csv(
      file = url, # Setting url 
      col_select = c(Date, HomeTeam, AwayTeam, FTHG, FTAG), # columns selection
      # Forcing the column types to avoid parsing issues
      col_types = cols(
        Date = col_character(),
        HomeTeam = col_character(),
        AwayTeam = col_character(),
        FTHG = col_integer(),
        FTAG = col_integer()
      ),
      # Handling duplicate column names by appending a suffix to make them unique
      name_repair = "unique_quiet",
      # No Debugging messages for column types
      show_col_types = FALSE
    )
  }) |>
  list_rbind() |>  # Combining all data frames into a single tibble
  filter(!is.na(Date) & Date != "") |>
  mutate(Date = dmy(Date))
serie_a_df

```

### Statistics for every team
```{r eval=TRUE, echo=TRUE}
# Creating Result column to track teams performance
serie_a_df <- serie_a_df |>
  mutate(Result = ifelse(FTHG == FTAG, "P", ifelse(FTHG > FTAG, "H", "A")))
serie_a_df

# Home matches performance
HomeCount <- serie_a_df |>
  count(HomeTeam, Result) |> 
  pivot_wider(names_from = Result, values_from = n, values_fill = 0)
HomeCount

# Away matches performance
AwayCount <- serie_a_df |>
  group_by(AwayTeam, Result) |> 
  summarise(n = n(), .groups = "drop") |> 
  pivot_wider(names_from = Result, values_from = n, values_fill = 0)
AwayCount

# Combining tables to compute stats
Stats <- full_join(HomeCount, AwayCount, join_by(HomeTeam==AwayTeam)) |>
  mutate(
    Wins = H.x + A.y,
    Draws  = P.x + P.y,
    Losses = A.x + H.y,
    Matches = Wins + Draws + Losses,
    Points = (Wins * 3) + (Draws * 1),
    PointsPerMatch = round(Points / Matches, 2)
  ) |>
  select(Team = HomeTeam, Matches, Wins, Draws, Losses, Points, PointsPerMatch) |>
  arrange(-PointsPerMatch)
Stats

```

### Research Questions
1. *Home Advantage*: How significant is the home-field advantage across Serie A history, and which teams display the largest performance gap between home and away matches?
2. *Goal-Scoring Trends*: Has the average number of goals per match changed significantly from 1993 to the present, reflecting an evolution toward more offensive or defensive tactics?
3. *Attack vs Defense*: Does defensive focus (fewer goals conceded) correlate more strongly with a high points-per-match average than offensive tactics (most goals scored)?
